claims.text: A machine-learning-potential-based ab initio molecular-dynamics method can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems while maintaining accuracy.
The proposed method can calculate free energies and relevant entropy terms for solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately describe the atomic interactions in the target systems.
Machine-learning potentials reduce computational cost by efficiently exploring the potential-energy surface.
The method maintains fidelity through the use of ab initio calculations.
The method will reduce computational cost by at least 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will be at least twice as fast as TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Predicted free energies and derived observables will agree with explicit ab initio results within ±5%.
The proposed method is applicable to systems containing up to 10 components.
The proposed method is applicable over temperatures from 500 K to 2000 K.
The method's accuracy may depend on the quality of its training data.
The method's accuracy may depend on potential transferability across systems and conditions.
Training and validating the method may require significant computational resources.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 50% cost reduction, at least a 2x TOR-TILD speedup, and ±5% accuracy, whereas the stated falsification rule only requires 30%, 1.5x, and ±10%. Thus results that fail the principal prediction could nevertheless avoid formal falsification.
